answer: I would like to talk about the person our whole family turns to in difficult times. The wisest person in my family is undoubtedly my grandmother, who despite having little formal education has an extraordinary understanding of people and life. She lives with my grandfather in our ancestral village home not far from Sirajganj, and we visit them often, especially during Eid, when the whole family gathers in the old house. What makes her so wise is not book knowledge but decades of hard-won experience, raising a large family through floods and lean years. She has this [[uncanny]] ability to sense when something is wrong, often before anyone says a word. Whenever the family faces a difficult decision, we instinctively turn to her, because her judgement is remarkably [[sound]]. She rarely tells you what to do; instead she asks the right questions and lets you reach your own conclusion. I think that is the mark of genuine wisdom, and it means you actually learn something. Her advice is always [[grounded]] in common sense rather than emotion, which is why it is so reliable. As for how she has helped me, over the years she has helped me through several tough moments simply by putting things in perspective. When I was nervous about starting my first job, she reminded me that everyone is a beginner once, and that honesty matters more than cleverness. Honestly, I treasure my conversations with her, and I know I will miss her [[counsel]] enormously one day.

followUps.answer: Fairly often, usually once or twice a month with my parents. The village is not far, so we can go for the day. Sitting with her on the veranda is one of the most [[tranquil]] parts of my month.

followUps.q: Do you think older people are wiser than younger people?
followUps.answer: Often, but not always. Age gives people experience, but wisdom depends on whether they reflect on it. Some young people are remarkably wise, and some older people never seem to learn.

note: Added opening, where she lives (ancestral village with grandfather, per persona), the source of her wisdom and a concrete example of her advice before my first job.
